## About

I am a Ph.D. student in the Department of Biostatistics at the UCLA Fielding School of Public Health, advised by [Dr. Christina Ramirez](https://ph.ucla.edu/about/faculty-staff-directory/christina-ramirez) and [Dr. Brunilda Balliu](https://brunildaballiu.github.io/).

My research interest is on interpretable machine learning methods for high-dimensional, correlated, and longitudinal data. I focus on tree-based models, network-aware feature selection, and unsupervised learning, with applications in HIV and aging, epigenomics, neuroscience, wearable devices and digital phenotyping for mental health.

Previously, I received my B.S. in Statistics from UC Davis (minors in Computer Science and Mathematics) in 2024. In my spare time, I enjoy running to bakeries and eating at them. I am on a mission to eat at every bakery in the westside of Los Angeles. I also am a big advocate for public transportation and will attempt to convince anyone near me to ride transit with me.

## R Package

<i class="bi bi-box-seam"></i> [**mossyforest**](https://timothyzshen.github.io/mossyforest/) — network-aware stability selection with random forests for correlated, high-dimensional data. (Methods Paper in progress)
